skills.name: agents-md
skills.description: AGENTS.md: create, shrink, or tend the current project's always-loaded file and docs/agents/ after a task when a non-discoverable fact is new, a line is stale or sprawling, or a pointer is missing; also `/agents-md` and `--force`.

skills.name: delegation
skills.description: Turn delegation mode on or off — you orchestrate, subagents execute — for this session, this project, or your user account.

skills.name: explain
skills.description: Explain the reply just given, or whatever the instruction names, better than it was explained the first time.

skills.name: commit
skills.description: Commit the working tree on the current branch, without pushing.

skills.name: orchestrate
skills.description: Work the tracker's ready-for-agent tickets unattended — claim, build, and independently verify them a wave at a time, integrating each wave into the current branch.

skills.name: push
skills.description: Follow commit, then push the current branch.

skills.name: ready-for-agent-check
skills.description: Read the tracker's ready-for-agent tickets the way an unattended builder will — one subagent per ticket, in a context that did not write it — and report what would stop that builder, before a run spends a wave finding out.

skills.name: release
skills.description: Ship a version — changelog, bump, push, tag, and GitHub release.

skills.name: cloudns
skills.description: Read and change DNS zones and records at ClouDNS on the user's behalf. Not for DNS at any other provider, not for registering, renewing or transferring domain names, and not for web hosting, email or SSL.

skills.name: hetzner
skills.description: Provision and operate Hetzner Cloud servers and deploy or maintain their websites and applications through hcloud, SSH, and cloud-init. Use for Hetzner Cloud infrastructure or workloads hosted there; excludes Robot dedicated servers and Object Storage.

skills.name: nodeping
skills.description: Read and change uptime monitoring at NodePing on the user's behalf — checks, results, contacts, schedules and notifications. Not for monitoring at any other provider, not for DNS, and not for server or site administration.

skills.name: postmark
skills.description: Inspect and change email at Postmark on the user's behalf — servers and message streams, domains and their DKIM and Return-Path records, sender signatures, templates, suppressions, bounces, delivery statistics, message search, webhooks, and a send the user asks for. Use for email at Postmark only; excludes other email providers, mailboxes, and setting DNS records.

skills.name: model-selector
skills.description: Choose the model and deliberation level that completes delegated work at the lowest total cost, or in the least time where the user has chosen time. Never used implicitly: a Skill that routes work runs its script.

skills.name: rename-invoices
skills.description: Safely plan and apply configurable filenames for text-based accounting PDFs.

skills.name: mirror
skills.description: Copy a web page, the pages under it that its links, sitemaps and feeds reach, and everything they need to display to disk, so they open in a browser with nothing fetched from the network.

features.name: session-cleanup
features.description: Leave the machine as the session found it — the agent records what it starts, and a lifecycle hook stops exactly that when the session ends or the next one begins.
writes: A fenced block, delimited by `<!-- kntnt.session-cleanup begin -->` and `<!-- kntnt.session-cleanup end -->`, at the end of each Harness's own global instruction file — `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `~/.codex/AGENTS.md`, `~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md`. These are files you own and read; everything above the fence is left exactly as it is, and disabling the Feature takes the fenced block away and nothing else.

One session-lifecycle entry per Harness, in that Harness's own hook table — `~/.claude/settings.json`, `~/.codex/hooks.json` — or, for OpenCode, as the plugin file `~/.config/opencode/plugins/kntnt.session-cleanup.js`.
Per-session manifests, a lock coordinating sweeps, and one log of every action taken, under `~/.kntnt/session-cleanup/`. Nothing is written outside these three places.

features.name: statusline
features.description: A two-line Claude Code status line — path, worktree, branch and working-tree state above; model, reasoning effort, context usage and subscription windows below.
writes: `statusLine` in `~/.claude/settings.json`, pointing at the shipped `statusline.sh` inside this collection's installed Manager. It is a single-valued setting, so it cannot hold two: where it already runs a command that is not this collection's, the row names that command and the confirmation asks whether to replace it, and nothing is written until you answer yes. Nothing is kept of what is replaced, so disabling the Feature afterwards clears the setting rather than restoring the command that was there. Disabling leaves the setting alone where this collection does not hold it.

`~/.kntnt/model-selector/quota.json`, this machine's weekly subscription window as Claude Code reported it on this render: the share used, when the window resets, how long the window is, and when the line was written. It is one filter over the payload already read — nothing is fetched and no credential could go in it — written to a temporary file beside its destination and moved into place, and any failure of it is swallowed and leaves the previous file standing. Model Selector's quota guard reads it, so Enabling this Feature is what arms that guard for the Claude channel and disabling it is what disarms it. Nothing is written where the payload carries no weekly window, which is every render before a session's first API response and every machine not on a Pro or Max plan.
